title: Quantum State of a Gravitating Spacetime Region
authors: Raphael Bousso, Sami Kaya, Guanda Lin, Arvin Shahbazi-Moghaddam
abstract: We associate a gravitational Hilbert space $\mathbf{H}_σ$ to any closed compact $(d-1)$-manifold $σ$ with real metric. A quantum state $\mathcal{J}(σ)$ is a $d$-manifold bounded by $σ$ and equipped with elliptic data. An inner product is defined by gluing states pairwise across $σ$ and evaluated by viewing the resulting closed $d$-manifold as a boundary condition on the gravitational path integral (GPI) over $(d+1)$-manifolds.   If $σ$ is nonempty and the GPI is dominated by a single $(d+1)$-manifold $M$ in the $G_N\to 0$ limit, then $M$ contains a Lorentzian CRT fixed-point set, providing $\mathcal{J}(σ)$ with a classical spacetime interpretation. Conversely, given a finite Lorentzian domain with edge $σ$, a state $\mathcal{J}(σ)$ may be associated to it by deforming its initial data off the real Lorentzian section and retaining only elliptic data. This establishes a broad correspondence between non-asymptotic spacetime regions and quantum states.   Assuming that $\mathbf{H}_σ$ factorizes over connected components of $σ$, our framework admits operators and partial traces. This allows us to explore the information-theoretic structure of the states we define. As an example, we construct a family of states by deforming partial Cauchy slices $Σ$ that straddle a two-sided black hole; $σ$ consists of two spheres. We construct the reduced state on one sphere and find that its Rényi entropies are positive, monotonic, and sensitive to all aspects of $Σ$ and its complex deformation. The von Neumann entropy, however, is controlled only by the maximin surface in the causal domain of $Σ$, independently of other parameters, so long as the complex deformation does not vanish. Our proposal may thus explain the efficacy of tensor network toy models of holography while transcending their limitations.
summary: This work proposes a novel framework linking quantum states in quantum gravity to specific, finite Lorentzian spacetime regions. It defines quantum states using elliptic data manifolds and calculates entanglement entropy by relating it to geometric quantities like the maximin surface area. This offers a powerful, general tool for exploring quantum information structure in regimes beyond standard holographic assumptions.
main_problem: The paper aims to establish a fundamental correspondence between quantum states defined on a boundary manifold and the geometry of finite Lorentzian spacetime regions in quantum gravity.
main_result: A broad correspondence is proposed linking quantum states $J(\sigma)$ to Lorentzian wedges $w_\sigma$, and the von Neumann entropy is shown to be controlled by the maximin surface area, echoing holographic principles.
method: The framework defines quantum states using elliptic data manifolds and calculates entanglement entropy via partial traces and the Gravitational Path Integral (GPI) evaluated on closed manifolds.
model_or_system: The system involves defining a gravitational Hilbert space $\mathbf{H}_\sigma$ associated with a compact boundary $\sigma$, and analyzing the quantum state $\mathcal{J}(\sigma)$ which is a $d$-manifold bounded by $\sigma$.
key_observables: Rényi entropies ($S_n$) and the von Neumann entropy ($S_1$), which are predicted to be proportional to the maximin surface area.
important_parameters: The gravitational coupling constant $G_N$, the dimension $d$, and the geometry of the boundary $\sigma$.
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the Hilbert space factorizes over connected components of $\sigma$, and the classical limit requires the GPI to be dominated by a single saddle geometry with Lorentzian fixed points.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the construction of quantum states via complex deformations from Lorentzian wedges, the calculation of reduced states via partial gluing, and the comparison of actions between Euclidean and Wall saddles.
paper_structure: The paper develops the mathematical framework by defining the Hilbert space and state structure, establishing the correspondence to classical spacetime regions, and then applying this structure to compute entanglement entropy for specific examples like black hole boundaries.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum gravity, the rigorous calculation of entanglement entropy via geometric quantities (maximin surface) and the development of a general state formalism are highly relevant to understanding quantum information structure in curved spacetime, which underpins many-body physics concepts.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Given a (d+1)-dimensional Lorentzian wedge wσ, we construct a (non-unique) quantum state J (σ) that gives rise to wσ in the classical limit. (a) A d-dimensional Cauchy slice Σ of wσ is deformed to a submanifold J(σ) in the complexification of wσ. In this example, the shared boundary σ of Σ and J(σ) has two components, σ = χ ⊔χc. (b) Of the full phase space data induced on J(σ), we retain only the conformal data ([hab], K) in the interior of J(σ), and the full (d −1)-metric γpq|σ on σ. These assignments turn J(σ) into an elliptic data manifold J (σ). — Conversely, we regard any elliptic data manifold J (σ), with arbitrary complex ([hab], K) and real γpq|σ, as a quantum state....
Figure 3. The closed elliptic data manifold trχ[˜ρ(χ, ¯χ)2] is obtained by cyclic gluing (here, across the vertical plane) of two copies of ˜ρ(χ, ¯χ) (see Fig. 2).

Figure 4. GPI with mixed-conformal boundary data. (a) On a closed d-manifold J(∅) = ∂M with (d −1)-dimensional submanifold ζ, we specify the full metric γpq on ζ and ([hab], K) on J(∅) \ ζ. Together, J(∅) and these data comprise the closed elliptic data manifold J (∅). In the example shown, ζ has two components, referred to as joints. The GPI is over spacetimes (M, gij) that induce these data on their boundary. (b) Local geometry at a joint ζ. The limiting outward normals n(−) and n(+) determine the exterior angle Θ. The illustrated joint is convex and has Θ > 0.

Figure 5. Elliptic data manifolds with boundary and their gluing. In panel (a), σ is connected: the underlying manifolds J(σ) and K(¯σ) are disks and glue across σ to form a sphere. In panel (b), σ = σ1⊔σ2 has two connected components: the underlying manifolds are cylinders and glue along both circular boundaries to form a torus. Cyan marks the gluing loci, blue and orange mark the data-equipped elliptic data manifolds J A(σ) and KA(¯σ), and the pale region shows one possible bulk filling M. The GPI sums over fillings. Setting K = J ∗gives G[(J ∗)AJ A] = ⟨J , J ⟩.

Figure 6. BTZ black hole of radius r1. A global maximal-volume slice (thin blue) with minimum radius ra < r1 contains the partial Cauchy slice Σ (thick blue), which is bounded by circles χ and χc at r = R in the left and right exteriors. A deformation of Σ off the real Lorentzian sector yields the underlying preparation manifold J(σ), with boundary σ = χ ⊔χc. Together with the induced mixed-conformal data, it defines the EDM J (σ).
